title: Quickstarts: standardize auth config + recommended timeouts; add troubleshooting
author: Wei Chen
body: Summary: Updates Redwood quickstarts to reflect the cross-SDK client behavior standard for authentication and timeout defaults. Adds a Troubleshooting section that specifically addresses the two most common issues we’ve seen in support escalations: missing/ambiguous API key configuration (SUP-9355) and streaming requests that appear to hang due to proxy buffering + insufficient read timeouts (SUP-9321). Motivation: As part of the SDK parity audit, we’re aligning auth + timeout semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go. Quickstarts were previously inconsistent (different env var names, mixed header examples, and missing guidance for connect/read/overall timeouts). This PR makes the docs match the new defaults and provides explicit guidance for enterprise/security reviewers (no file-based key lookup, redaction notes, least-privilege). Changes (high level): 1) Auth: Standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY for quickstarts, plus explicit constructor-based override examples in each language (do not encourage hardcoding). Call out that the SDKs send Authorization: Bearer <key> and that header casing is normalized by clients. 2) Timeouts: Add recommended baseline timeout values per request type (non-streaming vs streaming) and show how to override per-request where supported. Emphasize that streaming requires a long read timeout (or no read timeout) while still keeping an overall deadline for safety. 3) Troubleshooting: Add a dedicated section with copy-paste checks: confirm key is set, confirm base URL, inspect request-id header, handling 401 vs 403, and identifying proxy buffering symptoms for SSE. Notes: This PR intentionally avoids describing retry behavior in depth; retries are covered in the main docs PR and SDK changelogs. Quickstarts now link to the canonical behavior standard page (internal) and the public SDK docs page (once merged). Screenshots removed in favor of text snippets to reduce staleness. Backwards compatibility: Pure docs change; no runtime impact. Some snippets change env var names; we include a brief note that older snippets may reference RW_API_KEY and should be migrated to REDWOOD_API_KEY (aligns with SDK standardization work).
changed_areas: Timeout configuration snippets for streaming + non-streaming
New Troubleshooting section (request-id, 401/403, proxy buffering, timeouts)
Links updated to point to consolidated SDK docs pages
commits: docs(quickstarts): align auth env var + headers with SDK standard
docs(quickstarts): add recommended timeouts + per-request override examples
docs(troubleshooting): add request-id guidance and streaming/proxy notes
chore(markdown): normalize formatting and lint rules for callouts
notable_snippets: Auth (applies to all quickstarts): export REDWOOD_API_KEY="..."
TypeScript timeouts example: const client = new Redwood({ timeout: { connectMs: 5000, readMs: 60000, totalMs: 90000 }})
Go timeouts example: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 90*time.Second)  // streaming: keep read timeout high; prefer overall ctx deadline
Troubleshooting request-id note: "Include the x-request-id from the response headers when contacting support"
conversation: Elliot Price (review): Can we be more explicit about the header format and avoid implying multiple auth schemes? Also: please add a one-liner about not pasting API keys into screenshots/logs. Wei Chen (author): Updated wording to only reference Authorization: Bearer <key> and added a redaction note in Troubleshooting + Auth include. Ibrahim Khan (review): The timeout recommendations need to distinguish streaming vs non-streaming. For SSE, we should encourage an overall deadline but avoid short read timeouts. Wei Chen (author): Updated timeouts include to separate “non-streaming baseline” and “streaming baseline” and clarified that streaming often requires a long/disabled read timeout (while maintaining total). Marcus Lin (security): Please remove mention of reading keys from ~/.config or .env files in quickstarts. Security wants env var and explicit config only; no file discovery in docs until we have a vetted story. Wei Chen (author): Removed file-based language and replaced with env var + constructor override only. Also added a note: never commit keys; rotate if exposed. Sabrina James (review): Great to have a Troubleshooting section; can we add the proxy buffering symptom and a suggested mitigation? Wei Chen (author): Added a “Streaming appears stuck” entry with common proxy buffering behavior, and suggests disabling buffering for SSE or testing with curl to validate server-side streaming. Elliot Price (final): LGTM after the lint tweak; thanks for consolidating includes.
release_notes: Docs/Quickstarts: Auth examples now use REDWOOD_API_KEY consistently and describe Authorization: Bearer <key>. Added recommended timeout guidance for streaming vs non-streaming calls and a Troubleshooting section covering missing API keys, request-id collection, and common streaming/proxy buffering pitfalls.
